title: Fix the signal-handler lock release that resumes a running mutation unlocked
summary: Fix the confirmed F6-R10 blocker found by external review of the packaging stack: bin/agent-flow-kit traps INT and TERM with afk_lock_release and no exit, so bash runs the handler and resumes execution - a signal delivered mid-transaction frees the operation lock while the mutation keeps writing, and a second invocation can acquire the freed lock and mutate the same installation concurrently, violating the story's mutual-exclusion requirement. Repair the trap wiring so an interrupted run either stops cleanly through its rollback path or keeps holding the lock for the duration; the lock must never be released while this process can still write. Preserve the existing guarantees: the lock is still released on every genuine exit so a killed command never leaves the installation permanently busy, the recovery journal is still deliberately left visible for the next invocation, and all F6-R1 through F6-R9 semantics stay intact. Add deterministic regressions proving a signal during a live transaction cannot produce two concurrent writers or a freed lock with a live writer, and that normal exit, interrupt-before-lock, and interrupt-during-rollback still release exactly once. Run all Story 1.2 gates and git diff --check.
